description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, IKE, and ROME—across varying co-occurrence numbers, with the x-axis representing the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, and the y-axis showing accuracy in percentage from 30% to 55%. The Base method, represented by black circles connected by a solid line, starts at approximately 28.5% and remains relatively flat, ending at around 32.5%. The MEND method, shown with brown diamonds and a solid line, begins at about 36.5% and increases steadily to roughly 45.5%. The FT method, depicted with blue triangles and a solid line, starts at approximately 32.5% and rises to about 38.5%. The IKE method, marked by red triangles and a solid line, begins at around 32.5% and increases to approximately 41.5%. The ROME method, represented by green squares and a solid line, starts at about 43.5% and shows a consistent upward trend, reaching approximately 57.5%. Overall, the ROME method demonstrates the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence numbers, while the Base method shows the lowest.
